They play in the {{Welsh football updater|HolyTwn}}, the highest tier in the [[Welsh football league system]], having achieved promotion from the [[Cymru North]] in the [[2025-26 Cymru North|2025-26 season]].{{Cite web | date=2026-04-16| title=Holywell Town confirm promotion to the JD Cymru Premier |url=https://faw.cymru/cymru-leagues/news/holywell-town-confirm-promotion-to-the-jd-cymru-premier/ |access-date=2026-09-05 |website=faw.cymru}} The club plays its home matches at Halkyn Road, which is known as the ''Bartons North Wales Stadium''{{Cite web | date=2024-06-11| title=Holywell Town announce new sponsorship deal |url=https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=1011340190997594&set=a.531239402341011 |access-date=2026-09-05 |website=facebook.com}}{{Cite web | date=2026-06-27| title=2026-27 Ground Sponsor |url=https://x.com/HolywellTownFC/status/2070906018788262376 |access-date=2026-09-06 |website=x.com/HolywellTownFC}} for sponsorship purposes, and its nickname is '''"The Wellmen"'''. The club's traditional home shirt design is red and white vertical stripes. Holywell Town were a founding member of the [[Cymru Alliance]]{{Cite web | title=Cymru Alliance League 1990-2019 |url=https://www.welshsoccerarchive.co.uk/index.php/welsh-leagues/cymru-alliance |access-date=2026-09-05 |website=Welsh Football Data Archive}} and the [[1992-93 League of Wales|League of Wales]] (now the [[Cymru Premier]]), and recorded their highest top-flight finish of fifth position in the [[1993-94 League of Wales]]. Their promotion for the 2026-27 season marks their return to the Welsh top flight following [[1998-99 League of Wales|relegation in 1999]]. Since 2010, the club has won the [[FAW Trophy]] twice, in 2011{{Cite web | date=2020-04-24| title=Nine years on and Holywell Town's FAW Welsh Trophy victory is still as remarkable as ever
